arxiv-2110-04255.title: Celestial OPEs and 𝒘 𝟏 + ∞ w_{1+\infty} algebra from worldsheet in string theory
arxiv-2110-04255.creator: Hongliang Jiang
arxiv-2110-04255.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hongliang Jiang. Celestial operator product expansions (OPEs) arise from the collinear limit of scattering amplitudes and play a vital role in celestial holography. In this paper, we derive the celestial OPEs of massless fields in string theory from the worldsheet. By studying the worldsheet OPEs of vertex operators in worldsheet CFT and further examining their behaviors in the collinear limit, we find that new vertex operators for the massless fields in string theory are generated and become dominant in the collinear limit.

arxiv-2308-10628.title: Strangeness production in neutron star matter
arxiv-2308-10628.creator: Gao-Chan Yong 1,2
arxiv-2308-10628.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Gao-Chan Yong 1,2. Based on a dynamical model on particle production, the production and fraction of exotic components in neutron star matter are analyzed. It is found that there exists a small fraction of strangeness in twice saturation density matter. For five times saturation density matter, the fraction of strange baryons can be as high as 25-50%, depending on the equation of state used. The neutron-proton asymmetry of dense matter does not significantly impact the strangeness fraction in neutron star matter.

arxiv-2506-17931.title: IDAL: Improved Domain Adaptive Learning for Natural Images Dataset
arxiv-2506-17931.creator: Ravi Kant Gupta, Shounak Das, Amit Sethi
arxiv-2506-17931.description: Abstract We present a novel approach for unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) for natural images. A commonly-used objective for UDA schemes is to enhance domain alignment in representation space even if there is a domain shift in the input space. Existing adversarial domain adaptation methods may not effectively align different domains of multi-modal distributions associated with classification problems.

arxiv-2507-04596.title: Perturbed Toroidal Vortices Display Internal Simply Connected Topology
arxiv-2507-04596.creator: Taosif Ahsan, S.A. Cohen, A.H. Glasser
arxiv-2507-04596.description: Abstract This work shows that the interiors of perturbed zero-helicity vortices display simply connected topology with a crescent-shaped boundary. Flux surfaces in fluid and magnetic vortices were explored analytically, while particle trajectories in the context of plasma confinement were examined numerically, demonstrating the existence of both toroidal and simply connected topologies.

pmc-10620330.creator: Hong-xin Zhang
pmc-10620330.description: Objective Coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19) pandemic-related psychological symptoms can lead to smartphone addiction (SPA) risk and other behavioral disorders, thus impacting individuals’ mental health and well-being. The present study aims to propose a mediation model to investigate the association between emotional intelligence (EI) and SPA, and the mediating role of future anxiety (FA) during the post-COVID-19 era.

pmc-10855295.title: Costoclavicular Brachial Plexus Block Facilitates Painless Upper Extremity Reduction: A Case Report
pmc-10855295.creator: M Townsend Reeves, Katherine O’Neil, Todd L Slesinger
pmc-10855295.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). IntroductionThe costoclavicular brachial plexus block (CCBPB) has emerged as a more effective approach to regional anesthesia of the upper extremity. The costoclavicular space is the anterior portion of the superior thoracic aperture, located between the clavicle and first rib. The brachial plexus cords traverse this space clustered together in a superficial location lateral to the axillary artery and share a consistent topographical relationship to one another.

pmc-11310902.title: BMP-Binding Polysulfonate Brushes to Control Growth Factor Presentation and Regulate Matrix Remodelling
pmc-11310902.creator: Metzli
pmc-11310902.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs) are important targets to incorporate in biomaterial scaffolds to orchestrate tissue repair. Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) such as heparin allow the capture of BMPs and their retention at the surface of biomaterials at safe concentrations. Although heparin has strong affinities for BMP2 and BMP4, two important types of growth factors regulating bone and tissue repair, it remains difficult to embed stably at the surface of a broad range of biomaterials and degrades rapidly in vitro and in vivo.

pmc-11417591.creator: Eun Min Lee, Ju Hee Kim, Uiree Jo, Yoon Jung Cho
pmc-11417591.description: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis is a rare disease characterized by abnormal smooth muscle cell growth. It often accompanies tuberous sclerosis complex.

pmc-11628560.description: Fragmentomic features of circulating cell free mitochondrial DNA (ccf-mtDNA) including fragmentation profile, 5’ end base preference and motif diversity are poorly understood.
